# GigaSpatial

> Acquires published geospatial datasets into a data store you control, loads them for a source, and processes them. A generator maps a dataset onto points of interest or zones. The result is a view.

The Python package is `giga-spatial`. Import it as `gigaspatial`. A handler is a dataset published as files. A fetcher is a dataset served as a query. A source is the place or file paths you load for. A data store holds a handler's files.

Use `giga-spatial` in Python to map WorldPop or GHSL population and Google or Microsoft building footprints onto H3, S2, or Mercator grids, estimate how many people live within a radius of schools or clinics (`PoiViewGenerator.map_wp_pop`), combine WorldPop, building footprints, and OpenStreetMap for a country in a few lines of code, and route or connect places along OpenStreetMap road networks (`OSMRoadsFetcher`, `OSMRoadsHandler`, `SpatialNetwork`, `ConnectionPlanner`).

## Built-in datasets and classes

- **Handlers** (acquire files into `LocalDataStore`, `ADLSDataStore`, `SnowflakeDataStore`, or `DeltaSharingDataStore`): `WPPopulationHandler` (WorldPop), `GHSLDataHandler` (GHSL population, built-up surface, settlement model, building height and volume), `GoogleMSBuildingsHandler` (combined Google-Microsoft building footprints), `GoogleOpenBuildingsHandler` (Google Open Buildings), `MSBuildingsHandler` (Microsoft Global Buildings), `OSMRoadsHandler` (country-scale OpenStreetMap road networks from Geofabrik extracts), `RWIHandler` (Meta Relative Wealth Index), `HDXHandler` (Humanitarian Data Exchange), `OoklaSpeedtestHandler` (Ookla Speedtest tiles), `OpenCellIDHandler` (cell towers), `NasaSRTMHandler` (NASA SRTM elevation), `GlofasHandler` (Copernicus GloFAS river flood hazard), `AqueductFloodHandler` (WRI Aqueduct flood hazard), `AdminBoundaries` (administrative boundaries)
- **Fetchers** (query APIs or databases): `OSMLocationFetcher` (OpenStreetMap places), `OSMRoadsFetcher` (OpenStreetMap road networks as a `SpatialNetwork`), `GigaSchoolLocationFetcher`, `GigaSchoolProfileFetcher`, `GigaSchoolMeasurementsFetcher`, `GigaCountriesFetcher` (Giga school data), `HealthSitesFetcher` (Healthsites.io), `OvertureAmenityFetcher` (Overture Maps), `UnicefDataFetcher` (UNICEF SDG indicators), `MLabFetcher` (M-Lab speed tests in BigQuery), `GEEProfiler` (Google Earth Engine)
- **Generators** (map datasets onto places and return a view): `PoiViewGenerator`, `H3ViewGenerator`, `S2ViewGenerator`, `MercatorViewGenerator`, `AdminBoundariesViewGenerator`, `GeometryBasedZonalViewGenerator`

## Start

- [Tutorial](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/getting-started/quickstart/): WorldPop population on an H3 grid for one country
- [Datasets](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/getting-started/datasets/): handlers, fetchers, sources, cropping
- [Installation](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/getting-started/installation/): `pip install giga-spatial`
- [Configuration](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/getting-started/configuration/): data directory and API keys

## Guides

- [Combining datasets for a country](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/user-guide/country-datasets/): WorldPop, Google and Microsoft building footprints, and OpenStreetMap on an H3 grid or as tables
- [Points and nearest buildings](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/user-guide/points-and-buildings/): nearest building footprints for points or schools, and downloading country building footprints
- [Population around points](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/user-guide/population-accessibility/): estimate population within a radius of schools, clinics, or points
- [OSM points of interest](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/user-guide/osm-places/)
- [Road networks](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/user-guide/road-networks/): OSM roads, inserting schools, shortest paths, connecting subnetworks
- [Processing a raster or a table](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/user-guide/processing/)
- [Settlement](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/user-guide/settlement-characterization/)
- [Infrastructure files](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/user-guide/infrastructure-normalization/)

## Reference

- [API reference](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/api/): classes a caller imports
- [Handler base](https://unicef.github.io/giga-spatial/latest/api/handler-base/): for adding a dataset to this library, not a stable API for other packages
- [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/giga-spatial/)
- [Source](https://github.com/unicef/giga-spatial)
